newsitem.title: USA: Dura Automotive sees Q2 around consensus.
newsitem.headline: Dura Automotive sees Q2 around consensus.

text.p: Dura Automotive Systems Inc President Karl Storrie said Tuesday he was comfortable with second quarter earnings estimates around the First Call consensus of $0.57 a share.
"Those numbers are pretty close," Storrie said after a presentation at the Piper Jaffray investors conference here.
Year-ago second quarter results were not available. Dura, which makes mechanical assemblies and integrated systems for the global automotive industry, went public in August 1996.
Storrie said his company is "aggressively looking at acquisitions," mainly in the United States and Europe.
"We have five companies keyed in," Storrie said. "Two acquisition are reasonably close."
Dura is also looking to expand in Asia, mainly through its presence in Japan, but is not aggressively pursuing acquisitions in that region.
"We will probably first go through licensing arrangements and then joint ventures," Storrie said.
Dura is currently looking for that kind of arrangement with companies in Thailand and India, he added.
